title: Prognostic and predictive cytogenetic variants in hematological neoplasia
summary:
Treatment of blood cancer (leukemia and lymphoma) today is often based on certain changes detected in the DNA of cancer cells (genetic changes). 
This allows to characterize and classify these diseases. Treatment intensity depends on the risk of diseases progression and on the ability of directly targeting certain changes. Nevertheless a relevant number of patients die due to their disease even today. 
The results of this trial are going to deepen diagnostic abilities and help to further individualize treatment of patients with blood cancers. This in turn will help to improve their prognosis. 
Initially, the novel method of optical genome mapping will be used to detect structural genetic changes in the cancer cells. This data will be correlated to survival and response to treatment. In case that new genetic variants are found they will be subject to further functional analysis. 
If there are any hints, that results might be due to a hereditary disease, this will be proven by also analyzing healthy tissue from the patient. If needed, relatives then can be tested.
conditions: Other and unspecified types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma
Multiple myeloma and malignant plasma cell neoplasms
Other leukaemias of specified cell type
Other neoplasms of uncertain or unknown behaviour of lymphoid, haematopoietic and related tissue

interventions.name: Genetic diagnostics in hematological malignancies focussing on cytogenomics in myeloid neoplasm in correlation to prognosis and prediction to treatment

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- 18 years
- hematological malignancy (AML, MM, Lymphoma, MDS, MPN), 
- blood and/or bone marrow sampling
- informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- missing informed consent
- no hgematological neoplasia except for predictive testing of a first degree relative with proven germline variant
